_doc: Published meta-analyses reproduced from their own forest-plot rows by the harness pooling engine (harness/positive_control.py). A control is HELD only when its rows are read from bytes this repository holds; otherwise PENDING_SOURCE, never filled from memory.

controls.source: WHO REACT Working Group, JAMA 2020;324(13):1330-1341, PMID 32876694, PMC7489434 -- Figure 2 (28-day all-cause mortality, 7 trials)
controls.method: inverse-variance common effect; Paule-Mandel tau^2 with Hartung-Knapp interval
controls.why_pending: the per-trial rows are in Figure 2 of the full text, which is not held: Europe PMC fullTextXML is not available (not in the open-access subset), NCBI efetch db=pmc returns 'The publisher of this article does not allow downloading of the full text in XML form', the PMC page renders blank here and jamanetwork.com answers with a bot-verification page (not bypassed). The held comparator text (cache/corticosteroids-covid19-mortality/comparator_fulltext.txt) has the summaries but no per-trial rows.
controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the corticosteroids-covid19 topic (27 Sep 2026); consistent with the held text's summary OR 0.66 (0.53-0.82) fixed effect and 0.70 (0.48-1.01) random effects, I2 = 15.6%

controls.source: van Es et al., Blood 2014;124(12):1968-1975, PMID 24963045 -- recurrent VTE, 6 phase-3 DOAC-vs-VKA trials, from its supplementary counts
controls.method: inverse-variance common effect on log RR (tau^2 0); identified by exact reproduction
controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the doac-vte-recurrence topic (27 Sep 2026); consistent with the held comparator abstract RR 0.90 (95% CI 0.77-1.06)
controls.note: five rows are read from the trials' own held reports; Hokusai-VTE's on-treatment row (66/4,118 vs 80/4,122) is REPORTED_NOT_HELD, so the reproduction is conditional on that row. The comparator's text and supplement are not held.

controls.source: Ferracioli-Oda et al., PLoS One 2013;8(5):e63773, PMID 23691095 -- sleep latency, 15 studies, Figure 1
controls.method: inverse-variance fixed effect on the mean difference (the comparator states a fixed-effects model); rows are the figure's printed WMDs and 95% CIs
controls.expected_reported_by: the comparator's own figure and text (WMD 7.06, 95% CI 4.37 to 9.75); reproduced by the external melatonin review as 7.0606 (about 4.38-9.74)
controls.note: the published values print two decimals and the rows are themselves rounded, so agreement is within one unit of the last printed place, not exact; the figure's display errors (swapped weights, the objective subgroup interval) are flagged separately and do not touch this calculation

controls.source: Stefanou et al., Ther Adv Neurol Disord 2024, PMID 39345822, PMC11437580 -- MACE, 7 RCTs, Figure 2 (held image, CC BY-NC)
controls.method: DerSimonian-Laird random effects on log OR, 0.5 added to every cell of a single-zero study. Q 1.374405 < df 6, so the DL tau^2 is 0 and the DL estimate IS the inverse-variance common effect -- which our engine computes (synth.pool estimate_fixed); our engine implements no DL estimator (forbidden for k<10), so the control checks CE, tau^2 and Q
controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the semaglutide-obesity-mace topic (28 Sep 2026); consistent with the comparator's printed OR 0.79 (0.71-0.89), I2 0% (its own Mantel-Haenszel weights print SELECT at 97.4%)

controls.method: DerSimonian-Laird random effects on log RR from the plotted counts (the comparator's RevMan M-H random-effects plot); reproduced with a DL routine used only for published-analysis controls -- our pooling never uses DL
controls.source: Zhang et al., Front Endocrinol 2020, PMID 33519713, PMC7843571 -- heart failure hospitalization, 8 rows, Figure 2 (held image, CC BY), AS PRINTED (Zinman 2016 row arm-reversed)
controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the sglt2-primary-prevention-hf topic (28 Sep 2026); the comparator prints RR 0.63 (0.53-0.74), I2 = 74%

controls.method: DerSimonian-Laird random effects on log RR from the plotted counts (the comparator's RevMan M-H random-effects plot); reproduced with a DL routine used only for published-analysis controls -- our pooling never uses DL
controls.source: the same 8 rows with the Zinman 2016 (EMPA-REG OUTCOME) row replaced by its own report's counts

basis.quote: hospitalization for heart failure occurred in a significantly lower percentage of patients treated with empagliflozin [126/4687 patients (2.7%)] than with placebo [95/2333 patients (4.1%)]

controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the sglt2-primary-prevention-hf topic (28 Sep 2026): the single-row correction
controls.note: shows the comparator's I2 74% is produced by the arm reversal; our EMPA-REG hazard ratio is never altered to match

controls.source: Zhang et al., Front Cardiovasc Med 2025, PMID 40959489, PMC12434096 -- HFrEF all-cause mortality, 3 rows, Figure 4D (held image, CC BY)
controls.method: inverse-variance common (fixed) effect on log HR from the plot's printed log[HR] and SE (the comparator's RevMan 'IV, Fixed' plot); our engine's estimate_fixed
controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the spironolactone-hfref-mortality topic (28 Sep 2026); the comparator prints HR 0.78 (0.72-0.85), Chi2 = 3.53, df = 2, I2 = 43%
controls.note: a control of the ENGINE on the comparator's own rows; one of the three rows (EPHESUS) is outside our population, so this is not a check on our pooled result

controls.source: Ridker, Lonn, Paynter, Glynn, Yusuf. Circulation 2017;135:1979-1981, PMID 28385949, DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.117.028271 -- JUPITER + HOPE-3 participants aged >= 70, MI, stroke or cardiovascular death (3-point), 2 trials
controls.method: inverse-variance common effect on log HR over the two trials' age >= 70 hazard ratios
controls.expected_reported_by: external review of the statins-primary-prevention-elderly topic (28 Sep 2026); the letter prints HR 0.74 (0.61-0.91)
controls.note: an RCT checkpoint for the topic's question (randomised, primary prevention, older adults), NOT the registered comparator: Huang 2022 is observational. JUPITER is ours through its own older-adults report (PMID 20404379, a different, 5-component endpoint). HOPE-3 is not in our records at all: its age >= 70 stratum is published in this letter, the same kind of input as JUPITER's older-adults report, and our title-seeded search could not find it -- a discovery case, recorded, not acted on while the letter is not held.
